prompt:
You are a mathematician writing informal proofs that will later be formalised
in Agda by another agent. Write in ordinary mathematical English. Do not write
Agda. Do not skip steps by saying "clearly" or "trivially".


Follow the format of these examples exactly.

### Example 1

Informal statement:
For every natural number n, n + 0 = n.

Formal statement (Agda, for reference only):
+-identityr : (n : Nat) → n + 0 ≡ n

<INFORMAL_PROOF>
<STEP index="1" kind="induction">
We argue by induction on n.
</STEP>
<STEP index="2" kind="case">
Base case: when n is zero, 0 + 0 reduces to 0, so the two sides are equal.
</STEP>
<STEP index="3" kind="case">
Inductive case: suppose n + 0 = n. Then (suc n) + 0 reduces to suc (n + 0),
and rewriting with the induction hypothesis turns this into suc n.
</STEP>
</INFORMAL_PROOF>

### Example 2

Informal statement:
For all natural numbers m and n, m + suc n = suc (m + n).

Formal statement (Agda, for reference only):
+-suc : (m n : Nat) → m + suc n ≡ suc (m + n)

<INFORMAL_PROOF>
<STEP index="1" kind="induction">
We argue by induction on m, holding n fixed.
</STEP>
<STEP index="2" kind="case">
Base case: 0 + suc n reduces to suc n, and suc (0 + n) also reduces to suc n.
</STEP>
<STEP index="3" kind="case">
Inductive case: assume m + suc n = suc (m + n). Then (suc m) + suc n reduces
to suc (m + suc n), which by the induction hypothesis equals suc (suc (m + n)),
which is suc ((suc m) + n).
</STEP>
</INFORMAL_PROOF>

### Example 3

Informal statement:
Addition of natural numbers is commutative: m + n = n + m.

Formal statement (Agda, for reference only):
+-comm : (m n : Nat) → m + n ≡ n + m

<INFORMAL_PROOF>
<STEP index="1" kind="lemma" name="plusZeroRight">
First we need that n + 0 = n for every n; this is a separate induction and we
record it as its own lemma.
</STEP>
<STEP index="2" kind="lemma" name="plusSucRight">
We also need that m + suc n = suc (m + n) for all m and n; again a separate
induction, recorded as its own lemma.
</STEP>
<STEP index="3" kind="induction">
Now argue by induction on m.
</STEP>
<STEP index="4" kind="case">
Base case: 0 + n reduces to n, and n + 0 equals n by the first lemma.
</STEP>
<STEP index="5" kind="case">
Inductive case: assume m + n = n + m. Then suc m + n reduces to suc (m + n),
which by the hypothesis is suc (n + m), which by the second lemma is n + suc m.
</STEP>
</INFORMAL_PROOF>


### Now your turn

Informal statement:
For all natural numbers n and k with k ≤ n, the binomial coefficient n C′ k (the number of k-element subsets of an n-element set, equal to n! / (k! (n−k)!)) is symmetric: choosing k elements out of n is equivalent to discarding n − k of them, so n C′ (n − k) = n C′ k.

Formal statement (Agda, for reference only):
C′-sym : ∀ {n k} → k ≤ n → n C′ (n ∸ k) ≡ n C′ k


Rules:
- Output exactly one <INFORMAL_PROOF> block and nothing else after it.
- Each <STEP> gets an index, and a kind from: step, case, induction, lemma.
- Use kind="lemma" with a name="..." attribute for any step that deserves its
  own standalone proof. Prefer this for anything needing its own induction.
- Keep each step to one idea. Small steps are easier to formalise than big ones.
- Do not write Agda code inside the steps.
- Write each step once, as a finished answer. Do not deliberate, revise, or
  second-guess inside the steps; a step is a statement, not a search.
- Close the block with </INFORMAL_PROOF> and stop.

<STEP index="1" kind="step">
Fix natural numbers n and k with k ≤ n. Since k ≤ n, the truncated subtraction n ∸ k equals the ordinary difference n − k. Let X be a set with n elements, and for each j let S_j denote the family of j-element subsets of X, so that |S_j| = n C′ j. We must show |S_(n−k)| = |S_k|.
</STEP>
<STEP index="2" kind="lemma" name="complementSize">
For every subset A of X, the complement X \ A satisfies |X \ A| = n − |A|. Indeed, X is the disjoint union of A and X \ A, so n = |X| = |A| + |X \ A|. Subtracting |A| from both sides gives |X \ A| = n − |A|.
</STEP>
<STEP index="3" kind="lemma" name="complementInvolutive">
For every subset A of X, X \ (X \ A) = A. Take an element x. Then x ∈ X \ (X \ A) if and only if x ∈ X and x ∉ X \ A. The condition x ∉ X \ A means that it is not the case that both x ∈ X and x ∉ A. Since x ∈ X is assumed, this says x ∈ A. Hence x ∈ X \ (X \ A) if and only if x ∈ A. Because A ⊆ X, the elements of A are exactly the elements of X \ (X \ A) that lie in A, so the two sets are equal.
</STEP>
<STEP index="4" kind="lemma" name="complementMaps">
If A ∈ S_k then X \ A ∈ S_(n−k), and if B ∈ S_(n−k) then X \ B ∈ S_k. For the first claim, complementSize gives |X \ A| = n − k. For the second, complementSize gives |X \ B| = n − (n − k). Since k ≤ n, we have n − (n − k) = k, so |X \ B| = k.
</STEP>
<STEP index="5" kind="step">
Define f : S_k → S_(n−k) by f(A) = X \ A, and g : S_(n−k) → S_k by g(B) = X \ B. By complementMaps, both functions are well defined.
</STEP>
<STEP index="6" kind="step">
The map g is a two-sided inverse of f. For A ∈ S_k, g(f(A)) = X \ (X \ A), which equals A by complementInvolutive. For B ∈ S_(n−k), f(g(B)) = X \ (X \ B), which equals B by complementInvolutive.
</STEP>
<STEP index="7" kind="step">
Since f has a two-sided inverse, f is a bijection from S_k to S_(n−k). A bijection between finite sets gives equal cardinalities, so |S_k| = |S_(n−k)|, that is, n C′ k = n C′ (n − k).
</STEP>
<STEP index="8" kind="step">
Equality is symmetric, so n C′ (n − k) = n C′ k. Using n ∸ k = n − k from step 1, this is n C′ (n ∸ k) = n C′ k, as required.
</STEP>

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- The specification for combinatorics operations
------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- This module should not be imported directly! Please use
-- `Data.Nat.Combinatorics` instead.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Nat.Combinatorics.Specification where

open import Data.Bool.Base using (T; true; false)
open import Data.Nat.Base using (zero; suc; _≤ᵇ_; _≤_; _!; _∸_; pred;
  >-nonZero; _*_; NonZero; _+_; s≤s; z≤n; _>_)
open import Data.Nat.DivMod using (_/_; n/n≡1; /-congʳ; m*n/m!≡n/[m∸1]!;
  *-/-assoc; n/1≡n; m/n/o≡m/[n*o]; /-congˡ)
open import Data.Nat.Divisibility using (m≤n⇒m!∣n!; _∣_; ∣-refl;
  ∣-reflexive; module ∣-Reasoning; ∣m∣n⇒∣m+n; *-monoʳ-∣; m∣n/o⇒o*m∣n)
open import Data.Nat.Properties
open import Data.Nat.Combinatorics.Base using (_P′_; _P_; _C′_; _C_)
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Relation.Nullary.Decidable using (yes; no; does)
open import Relation.Nullary.Negation using (contradiction)
open import Relation.Binary.PropositionalEquality.Core
  using (_≡_; trans; _≢_; subst; refl; sym; cong; cong₂)

import Algebra.Properties.CommutativeSemigroup *-commutativeSemigroup as *-CS

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Prelude

private
  ≤ᵇ⇒≤′ : ∀ {m n} → (m ≤ᵇ n) ≡ true → m ≤ n
  ≤ᵇ⇒≤′ {m} {n} eq = ≤ᵇ⇒≤ m n (subst T (sym eq) _)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties of _P′_

nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! : ∀ {n k} → k ≤ n → n P′ k ≡ (n ! / (n ∸ k) !) {{(n ∸ k) !≢0}}
nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! {n} {zero}  z≤n = sym (n/n≡1 (n !) {{n !≢0}})
nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! {n} {suc k} k<n = begin-equality
  (n ∸ k) * (n P′ k)             ≡⟨ cong ((n ∸ k) *_) (nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! (<⇒≤ k<n)) ⟩
  (n ∸ k) * (n ! / (n ∸ k) !)    ≡⟨ *-/-assoc (n ∸ k) (m≤n⇒m!∣n! (m∸n≤m n k)) ⟨
  (((n ∸ k) * n !) / (n ∸ k) !)  ≡⟨ m*n/m!≡n/[m∸1]! (n ∸ k) (n !) ⟩
  (n ! / (pred (n ∸ k) !))       ≡⟨ /-congʳ (cong _! (pred[m∸n]≡m∸[1+n] n k)) ⟩
  (n ! / (n ∸ suc k) !)          ∎
  where
  open ≤-Reasoning
  instance
    _ = (n ∸ k) !≢0
    _ = (pred (n ∸ k)) !≢0
    _ = (n ∸ suc k) !≢0
    _ = >-nonZero (m<n⇒0<n∸m k<n)

nP′k≡n[n∸1P′k∸1] : ∀ n k → .{{NonZero n}} → .{{NonZero k}} →
                   n P′ k ≡ n * (pred n P′ pred k)
nP′k≡n[n∸1P′k∸1] n           (suc zero)            = refl

------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- This module should not be imported directly! Please use
-- `Data.Nat.Combinatorics` instead.

open import Data.Bool.Base using (T; true; false)
open import Data.Nat.Base using (zero; suc; _≤ᵇ_; _≤_; _!; _∸_; pred;
  >-nonZero; _*_; NonZero; _+_; s≤s; z≤n; _>_)
open import Data.Nat.DivMod using (_/_; n/n≡1; /-congʳ; m*n/m!≡n/[m∸1]!;
  *-/-assoc; n/1≡n; m/n/o≡m/[n*o]; /-congˡ)
open import Data.Nat.Divisibility using (m≤n⇒m!∣n!; _∣_; ∣-refl;
  ∣-reflexive; module ∣-Reasoning; ∣m∣n⇒∣m+n; *-monoʳ-∣; m∣n/o⇒o*m∣n)
open import Data.Nat.Properties
open import Data.Nat.Combinatorics.Base using (_P′_; _P_; _C′_; _C_)
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Relation.Nullary.Decidable using (yes; no; does)
open import Relation.Nullary.Negation using (contradiction)
open import Relation.Binary.PropositionalEquality.Core
  using (_≡_; trans; _≢_; subst; refl; sym; cong; cong₂)

import Algebra.Properties.CommutativeSemigroup *-commutativeSemigroup as *-CS

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Prelude

private
  ≤ᵇ⇒≤′ : ∀ {m n} → (m ≤ᵇ n) ≡ true → m ≤ n

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties of _P′_

nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! : ∀ {n k} → k ≤ n → n P′ k ≡ (n ! / (n ∸ k) !) {{(n ∸ k) !≢0}}
nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! {n} {zero}  z≤n = sym (n/n≡1 (n !) {{n !≢0}})
nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! {n} {suc k} k<n = begin-equality
  (n ∸ k) * (n P′ k)             ≡⟨ cong ((n ∸ k) *_) (nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! (<⇒≤ k<n)) ⟩
  (n ∸ k) * (n ! / (n ∸ k) !)    ≡⟨ *-/-assoc (n ∸ k) (m≤n⇒m!∣n! (m∸n≤m n k)) ⟨
  (((n ∸ k) * n !) / (n ∸ k) !)  ≡⟨ m*n/m!≡n/[m∸1]! (n ∸ k) (n !) ⟩
  (n ! / (pred (n ∸ k) !))       ≡⟨ /-congʳ (cong _! (pred[m∸n]≡m∸[1+n] n k)) ⟩
  (n ! / (n ∸ suc k) !)          ∎
  where
  open ≤-Reasoning
  instance
    _ = (n ∸ k) !≢0
    _ = (pred (n ∸ k)) !≢0
    _ = (n ∸ suc k) !≢0
    _ = >-nonZero (m<n⇒0<n∸m k<n)

nP′k≡n[n∸1P′k∸1] : ∀ n k → .{{NonZero n}} → .{{NonZero k}} →
                   n P′ k ≡ n * (pred n P′ pred k)
nP′k≡n[n∸1P′k∸1] n           (suc zero)            = refl
nP′k≡n[n∸1P′k∸1] n@(suc n-1) k@(suc k-1@(suc k-2)) = begin-equality
  n P′ k                        ≡⟨⟩
  (n ∸ k-1) * (n P′ k-1)        ≡⟨ cong ((n ∸ k-1) *_) (nP′k≡n[n∸1P′k∸1] n k-1) ⟩
  (n ∸ k-1) * (n * (n-1 P′ k-2))  ≡⟨ x∙yz≈y∙xz (n ∸ k-1) n (n-1 P′ k-2) ⟩
  n * ((n ∸ k-1) * (n-1 P′ k-2))  ≡⟨⟩
  n * (n-1 P′ k-1)              ∎
  where open ≤-Reasoning; open *-CS

P′-rec : ∀ {n k} → k ≤ n → .{{NonZero k}} →
        n P′ k ≡ k * (pred n P′ pred k) + pred n P′ k
P′-rec n@{suc n-1} k@{suc k-1} k≤n = begin-equality
  n P′ k                                        ≡⟨ nP′k≡n[n∸1P′k∸1] n k ⟩
  n * (n-1 P′ k-1)                              ≡⟨ cong (_* (n-1 P′ k-1)) (m+[n∸m]≡n {k} {n} k≤n) ⟨
  (k + (n ∸ k)) * (n-1 P′ k-1)                  ≡⟨ *-distribʳ-+ (n-1 P′ k-1) k (n ∸ k) ⟩
  k * (n-1 P′ k-1) + (n-1 ∸ k-1) * (n-1 P′ k-1) ≡⟨⟩
  k * (n-1 P′ k-1) + (n-1 P′ k)                 ∎
  where open ≤-Reasoning

nP′n≡n! : ∀ n → n P′ n ≡ n !

  n P′ n          ≡⟨ nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! (≤-refl {n}) ⟩
  n ! / (n ∸ n) ! ≡⟨ /-congʳ (cong _! (n∸n≡0 n)) ⟩
  n ! / 0 !       ≡⟨⟩
  n ! / 1         ≡⟨ n/1≡n (n !) ⟩
  n !             ∎
  where open ≤-Reasoning; instance _ = (n ∸ n) !≢0

k!∣nP′k {n}         {zero}      k≤n = ∣-refl
k!∣nP′k n@{suc n-1} k@{suc k-1} k≤n@(s≤s k-1≤n-1) with k-1 ≡? n-1
... | yes refl = ∣-reflexive (sym (nP′n≡n! n))
... | no  k≢n  = begin
  k !                           ≡⟨⟩
  k * k-1 !                     ∣⟨ ∣m∣n⇒∣m+n (*-monoʳ-∣ k (k!∣nP′k k-1≤n-1)) ( k!∣nP′k (≤∧≢⇒< k-1≤n-1 k≢n)) ⟩
  k * (n-1 P′ k-1) + (n-1 P′ k) ≡⟨ P′-rec k≤n ⟨
  n P′ k                        ∎
  where open ∣-Reasoning

[n∸k]!k!∣n! : ∀ {n k} → k ≤ n → (n ∸ k) ! * k ! ∣ n !

  (subst (k ! ∣_) (nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! k≤n) (k!∣nP′k k≤n))
  where instance _ = (n ∸ k) !≢0

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties of _P_

... | true  = nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! k≤n
... | false = contradiction (≤⇒≤ᵇ k≤n) (subst T eq)

k>n⇒nPk≡0 : ∀ {n k} → k > n → n P k ≡ 0

... | true  = contradiction (≤ᵇ⇒≤′ eq) (<⇒≱ k>n)
... | false = refl

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties of _C′_

-- dsp: lemmas
postulate
  Csym-gap0 : (n k : ℕ) → k ≤ n → n ∸ (n ∸ k) ≡ k

-- dsp: end of lemmas
C′-sym : ∀ {n k} → k ≤ n → n C′ (n ∸ k) ≡ n C′ k

-- Steps 2–5: complementMaps sends S_k to S_(n−k) (its size is n − |A|), and complementBack sends S_(n−k) to S_k using n − (n − k) = k. Define f = complementMaps and g = complementBack.
-- Steps 6–7: complementInvolutive and complementInvolutiveRight make g and f two-sided inverses. cardBijection then gives |S_k| = |S_(n−k)|, that is n C′ k = n C′ (n − k).
-- Step 8: equality is symmetric, and n ∸ k = n − k from step 1, so n C′ (n ∸ k) = n C′ k.
C′-sym {n} {k} k≤n = (Csym-gap0 n)

open import Data.Nat.Base using (zero; suc; _≤ᵇ_; _≤_; _!; _∸_; pred;

open import Data.Nat.DivMod using (_/_; n/n≡1; /-congʳ; m*n/m!≡n/[m∸1]!;
  *-/-assoc; n/1≡n; m/n/o≡m/[n*o]; /-congˡ)
open import Data.Nat.Divisibility using (m≤n⇒m!∣n!; _∣_; ∣-refl;
  ∣-reflexive; module ∣-Reasoning; ∣m∣n⇒∣m+n; *-monoʳ-∣; m∣n/o⇒o*m∣n)
open import Data.Nat.Properties
open import Data.Nat.Combinatorics.Base using (_P′_; _P_; _C′_; _C_)
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Relation.Nullary.Decidable using (yes; no; does)

open import Relation.Binary.PropositionalEquality.Core

import Algebra.Properties.CommutativeSemigroup *-commutativeSemigroup as *-CS

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Prelude

private
  ≤ᵇ⇒≤′ : ∀ {m n} → (m ≤ᵇ n) ≡ true → m ≤ n

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties of _P′_

nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! : ∀ {n k} → k ≤ n → n P′ k ≡ (n ! / (n ∸ k) !) {{(n ∸ k) !≢0}}
nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! {n} {zero}  z≤n = sym (n/n≡1 (n !) {{n !≢0}})
nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! {n} {suc k} k<n = begin-equality
  (n ∸ k) * (n P′ k)             ≡⟨ cong ((n ∸ k) *_) (nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! (<⇒≤ k<n)) ⟩
  (n ∸ k) * (n ! / (n ∸ k) !)    ≡⟨ *-/-assoc (n ∸ k) (m≤n⇒m!∣n! (m∸n≤m n k)) ⟨
  (((n ∸ k) * n !) / (n ∸ k) !)  ≡⟨ m*n/m!≡n/[m∸1]! (n ∸ k) (n !) ⟩
  (n ! / (pred (n ∸ k) !))       ≡⟨ /-congʳ (cong _! (pred[m∸n]≡m∸[1+n] n k)) ⟩
  (n ! / (n ∸ suc k) !)          ∎
  where
  open ≤-Reasoning
  instance
    _ = (n ∸ k) !≢0
    _ = (pred (n ∸ k)) !≢0
    _ = (n ∸ suc k) !≢0
    _ = >-nonZero (m<n⇒0<n∸m k<n)

nP′k≡n[n∸1P′k∸1] : ∀ n k → .{{NonZero n}} → .{{NonZero k}} →
                   n P′ k ≡ n * (pred n P′ pred k)
nP′k≡n[n∸1P′k∸1] n           (suc zero)            = refl
nP′k≡n[n∸1P′k∸1] n@(suc n-1) k@(suc k-1@(suc k-2)) = begin-equality
  n P′ k                        ≡⟨⟩
  (n ∸ k-1) * (n P′ k-1)        ≡⟨ cong ((n ∸ k-1) *_) (nP′k≡n[n∸1P′k∸1] n k-1) ⟩
  (n ∸ k-1) * (n * (n-1 P′ k-2))  ≡⟨ x∙yz≈y∙xz (n ∸ k-1) n (n-1 P′ k-2) ⟩
  n * ((n ∸ k-1) * (n-1 P′ k-2))  ≡⟨⟩
  n * (n-1 P′ k-1)              ∎
  where open ≤-Reasoning; open *-CS

P′-rec : ∀ {n k} → k ≤ n → .{{NonZero k}} →
        n P′ k ≡ k * (pred n P′ pred k) + pred n P′ k
P′-rec n@{suc n-1} k@{suc k-1} k≤n = begin-equality
  n P′ k                                        ≡⟨ nP′k≡n[n∸1P′k∸1] n k ⟩
  n * (n-1 P′ k-1)                              ≡⟨ cong (_* (n-1 P′ k-1)) (m+[n∸m]≡n {k} {n} k≤n) ⟨
  (k + (n ∸ k)) * (n-1 P′ k-1)                  ≡⟨ *-distribʳ-+ (n-1 P′ k-1) k (n ∸ k) ⟩
  k * (n-1 P′ k-1) + (n-1 ∸ k-1) * (n-1 P′ k-1) ≡⟨⟩
  k * (n-1 P′ k-1) + (n-1 P′ k)                 ∎
  where open ≤-Reasoning

nP′n≡n! : ∀ n → n P′ n ≡ n !

  n P′ n          ≡⟨ nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! (≤-refl {n}) ⟩
  n ! / (n ∸ n) ! ≡⟨ /-congʳ (cong _! (n∸n≡0 n)) ⟩
  n ! / 0 !       ≡⟨⟩
  n ! / 1         ≡⟨ n/1≡n (n !) ⟩
  n !             ∎
  where open ≤-Reasoning; instance _ = (n ∸ n) !≢0

k!∣nP′k : ∀ {n k} → k ≤ n → k ! ∣ n P′ k
k!∣nP′k {n}         {zero}      k≤n = ∣-refl
k!∣nP′k n@{suc n-1} k@{suc k-1} k≤n@(s≤s k-1≤n-1) with k-1 ≡? n-1
... | yes refl = ∣-reflexive (sym (nP′n≡n! n))
... | no  k≢n  = begin
  k !                           ≡⟨⟩
  k * k-1 !                     ∣⟨ ∣m∣n⇒∣m+n (*-monoʳ-∣ k (k!∣nP′k k-1≤n-1)) ( k!∣nP′k (≤∧≢⇒< k-1≤n-1 k≢n)) ⟩
  k * (n-1 P′ k-1) + (n-1 P′ k) ≡⟨ P′-rec k≤n ⟨
  n P′ k                        ∎
  where open ∣-Reasoning

[n∸k]!k!∣n! : ∀ {n k} → k ≤ n → (n ∸ k) ! * k ! ∣ n !
[n∸k]!k!∣n! {n} {k} k≤n = m∣n/o⇒o*m∣n (m≤n⇒m!∣n! (m∸n≤m n k))
  (subst (k ! ∣_) (nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! k≤n) (k!∣nP′k k≤n))
  where instance _ = (n ∸ k) !≢0

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties of _P_

nPk≡n!/[n∸k]! : ∀ {n k} → k ≤ n → n P k ≡ (n ! / (n ∸ k) !) {{(n ∸ k) !≢0}}
nPk≡n!/[n∸k]! {n} {k} k≤n with k ≤ᵇ n in eq
... | true  = nP′k≡n!/[n∸k]! k≤n
... | false = contradiction (≤⇒≤ᵇ k≤n) (subst T eq)

k>n⇒nPk≡0 : ∀ {n k} → k > n → n P k ≡ 0
k>n⇒nPk≡0 {n} {k} k>n with k ≤ᵇ n in eq
... | true  = contradiction (≤ᵇ⇒≤′ eq) (<⇒≱ k>n)
... | false = refl

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties of _C′_

-- dsp: lemmas
postulate

postulate

-- dsp: end of lemmas
C′-sym : ∀ {n k} → k ≤ n → n C′ (n ∸ k) ≡ n C′ k
-- Step 1: Fix natural numbers n and k with k ≤ n. Let S be a set with exactly n elements, and let 𝒫_j be the collection of j-element subsets of S.
-- Step 2: Since k ≤ n, n ∸ k is n − k, and n − (n − k) = k, so the claim is that 𝒫_{n−k} and 𝒫_k have the same number of elements.
-- Step 5: Define f from 𝒫_k to 𝒫_{n−k} by f(A) = S∖A. It is well-defined by complementSize, since |S∖A| = n − k.
-- Step 6: Define g from 𝒫_{n−k} to 𝒫_k by g(B) = S∖B. It is well-defined by complementSize and complementInvolutive, since |S∖B| = n − (n − k) = k.
-- Step 7: g and f are mutually inverse by complementInvolutive, so f is a bijection from 𝒫_k to 𝒫_{n−k}.
-- Step 8: A bijection between finite sets gives |𝒫_k| = |𝒫_{n−k}|, that is n C′ k = n C′ (n − k) = n C′ (n ∸ k).
C′-sym {n} {k} k≤n = {!!}

lemmas.name: complementSize
lemmas.signature: ∀ {n k} → k ≤ n → (n ∸ k) + k ≡ n
lemmas.informal_hint: For every subset A of S, the complement S∖A satisfies |A| + |S∖A| = n. Proof: each element of S lies in exactly one of A and S∖A, so S is the disjoint union of A and S∖A. The number of elements of a disjoint union is the sum of the numbers of elements of its parts. Hence |A| + |S∖A| = |S| = n.

lemmas.name: complementInvolutive
lemmas.signature: ∀ {n k} → k ≤ n → n ∸ (n ∸ k) ≡ k
lemmas.informal_hint: For every subset A of S, the complement of the complement is A, that is S∖(S∖A) = A. Proof: an element x lies in S∖(S∖A) exactly when x ∈ S and x ∉ S∖A.
